title.narrative: Response to the Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals and Host Community (EA/2024)

description.narrative:
In 2024, 7 years after the exodus of Rohingya from Myanmar, nearly 1 million refugees are still living in temporary settlements spread across 33 congested camps in Cox’s Bazar District, Bangladesh. In August 2024, escalating violence forced greater numbers of Rohingya civilians to flee across the border, further increasing pressure on the services in the camps. In their current circumstances, the refugees lack formal legal status, face extreme restrictions on movement and are not permitted to legally work. The refugee influx has overwhelmed the existing response capacity and put immense strain on infrastructure, services, resources and the local environment, and the extreme level of humanitarian needs has not decreased. The Government of Bangladesh and local communities have supported the refugees to the best of their ability, but solidarity has been increasingly strained as global attention shifts to new conflicts and crises.
Caritas Bangladesh (CB) was one of the first humanitarian actors to respond in 2017, Despite decreasing funding, it has been continuously responding to the emergency needs of Rohingya refugees since then. They have provided shelter, food, Non-Food Items, site improvements, WASH, education, livelihoods support, and have implemented disaster risk reduction initiatives. CB has also supported community-based protection which has become an urgent focus in the past months. Reductions in funding support, a lack of livelihood options, human trafficking and continuing violence in Myanmar have resulted in growing frustration and hopelessness. This has led to even higher levels of insecurity and violence in the camps.
Over the last 7 years Caritas Bangladesh has reached well over a 1 million people. This contribution will go towards CB's 2024 emergency appeal which will support 117,610 people in Cox's Bazar.
